desks.title: Customer Support — H1 headcount and coverage plan
desks.description: Eight roles to fill before the billing platform migration: the hiring pipeline, the coverage maths behind each seat, and the ramp risk the team leads are watching.
desks.brief:
## Customer Support — H1 headcount and coverage plan

**Department** Customer Support · 28 agents in three teams · five leads
**Approved** 6 new seats + 2 backfills · $580k fully loaded
**Deadline** billing platform migration goes live @+63d

### Why we're hiring
Weekly contacts run at about 4,600, roughly 164 per agent. The billing migration is forecast to lift that to 5,600 for at least a quarter (+22%). At the same rate that needs 34 agents. Joel and Ana have resigned, so 26 stay: six new seats plus two backfills gets us to 34.

### Where the gaps are
- **Evenings 17:00–21:00** — 19% of contacts, 4 agents rostered
- **Weekends** — the billing queue waits until Monday
- **L2 technical** — escalations wait 2.5 days on average

### Shared with
The five leads, Kemi in recruiting and Tamsin in finance. Hiring leads move their own roles through the stages here, so the Friday hiring-status email has stopped.

### Where it stands
One role filled, two offers out, two in interviews. Plan cost is $556k, $24k under approval. New agents take six weeks to ramp, so **only the first billing hire will be fully productive at go-live**.

callout.title: Risk: billing ramp misses go-live
callout.body: Only one of three billing hires is ramped by go-live @+63d. Proposal: lend three onboarding agents to billing for the first four weeks after go-live. Needs Rosa's sign-off by @+3d.

children.label: Escalation form in the help desk

blocks.h3: How many agents do we need?

blocks.p: Built from the last 12 weeks of contact data. Kwame owns the forecast and checks the evening peak with an Erlang C queue model; the leads check it before any hiring decision moves forward.

ul: Contacts today: about 4,600 a week across chat, email and phone
Handled per agent: about 164 a week at 80% occupancy
Forecast after go-live: about 5,600 a week (+22%) for at least a quarter
5,600 ÷ 164 = 34 agents. We have 28, and two are leaving

blocks.p: Billing gets three because the migration lands there first. Technical gets an L2 seat to stop escalations waiting 2.5 days, an evening seat, and Joel's backfill. Onboarding gets the enterprise seat and Ana's backfill.

ul: Contacts land under 5,200 a week → hold the evening tech seat
Rewritten articles deflect more than 5% → hold the weekend billing seat
Go-live slips past @+63d → keep the start dates and use the extra ramp time

blocks.quote: Hire for the forecast, but keep two seats conditional: the evening tech seat on go-live volume, the weekend billing seat on what the rewritten articles deflect.

notes.title: Leads sync — what I heard
notes.body:
From this week's leads sync:

- Tomás wants the early-shift offer signed now — the candidate has a competing offer
- Aiko rates the L2 seat above the evening seat; happy to hold the evening seat if volume lands low
- Rosa can lend three onboarding agents, but not in the last week of the month (enterprise go-lives)
- Kemi can run two interview panels a week, not three

To decide: can the loan dates dodge Rosa's month-end?

notes.title: Finance check-in with Tamsin
notes.body:
- $580k is fully loaded: salary plus 15% on-costs
- Backfills don't need re-approval; new seats do if a start date slips a full quarter
- Seat costs are at base rates, so evening and weekend penalty rates are not in the $556k yet
- Can the $24k headroom fund those penalty rates plus overtime during the ramp? She'll confirm by @+5d

desks.title: Support goals — weekly leads review and 1:1s
desks.description: Eight key results across three objectives, updated by the leads before Monday's review, with each lead's 1:1 agenda and the upward update drawn from the same numbers.
desks.brief:
## Support goals — week 8 of 13

**Leads** Tomás (Billing) · Aiko (Technical) · Rosa (Onboarding) · Nadia (Quality & knowledge) · Kwame (Workforce)
**Review** Mondays 10:00, 20 minutes
**Quarter ends** @+35d

### Objectives
1. **Faster answers** — customers hear back sooner, especially on billing
2. **Better answers** — fewer reopened tickets, higher CSAT
3. **Migration ready** — every agent certified, runbook signed off before go-live

### How the review works
Each lead updates their rows before 10:00: what the number is now, progress and status. The meeting covers only rows that are **At risk** or **Off track**, and each one ends with a decision or an owner. It used to be 45 minutes of read-outs with a slide per lead; it now runs 20 and the slides are gone.

### Where it stands
Five of eight key results on track. CSAT and agent certification are at risk; help-article rewrites are off track. Average progress is 64% against 62% expected at week 8 — on pace overall, but uneven: faster answers is well ahead, the other two objectives are behind.

callout.title: Off track: help-article rewrites
callout.body: 14 of 40 articles done at week 8. The other 26 in five weeks means 5.2 a week; the pace so far is under two. Nadia is the only writer and spends four days a week on QA. Decision for Monday: two protected writing days for her until quarter end, with QA sampling moving to the leads.

rows.kr: 95% of onboarding calls booked within 2 days
All 26 agents certified on new billing

children.label: Ready to lead a bigger team?
Forecast sheet the leads can read

blocks.p: Twenty minutes. Rows are updated before we start; we discuss only what is At risk or Off track, and every discussion ends in a decision or an owner.

ul: CSAT: Nadia to tag the last 60 low scores by cause before the next review
Certification: Tomás to run two pair-certification sessions a week
Evening tech seat stays on hold until go-live volume is known
Backlog target stays at 150 — Tomás thinks 100 is reachable; revisit at week 10
Kwame posts the first-response chart in the team channel every Friday

ol: Update your rows before the meeting, not in it
Anything on track for three weeks running drops off the agenda

notes.title: Upward update — 1:1 with the COO
notes.body:
Three lines, straight from the rows on this desk:

- Faster answers is ahead: first response down from 4.0h to 1.4h, backlog down from 640 to 290
- Better answers is behind: articles off track (14 of 40), CSAT at 90% against a 92% target
- Migration readiness hinges on certification — 9 of 26 agents so far

If protected writing days haven't moved the articles by week 10, ask for a contract writer for six weeks.
